subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: Should sandboxed subagent startup failures be reported through the accepted async run path with a typed terminal startup-failure state, or should `sessions_spawn` preflight sandbox startup before returning accepted?
rationale: Both shapes can fix the zero-token hang, but they have different compatibility and lifecycle semantics for gateway callers, session state, and existing async spawn behavior.

options.title: Terminalize async startup failures
options.body: Keep `sessions_spawn` async acceptance behavior and add a typed startup-failed terminal state plus visible logs/session metadata for Docker sandbox startup failures.

options.title: Preflight sandbox before accept
options.body: Resolve and start the sandbox before returning `accepted`, making spawn failures immediate but changing the existing async contract and latency profile.

options.title: Defer to lifecycle PR only
options.body: Let the broader lifecycle work define first-progress/startup-failed semantics before changing the sandbox-specific path, while keeping this issue as the Docker proof case.

recommendation.title: Terminalize async startup failures
recommendation.body: Keep `sessions_spawn` async acceptance behavior and add a typed startup-failed terminal state plus visible logs/session metadata for Docker sandbox startup failures.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history signal is around subagent lifecycle and spawn planning, which owns the async-versus-preflight contract choice.
